messages:
maria_sales: Heads-up — Globex POC stalled. App hosts in prod subnet can't finish TLS to our private endpoint. Works from jumpbox. They see TLS alert and 'unknown ca' in app logs. Customer says this started after they enabled perimeter TLS inspection.

ash_se: Oof. Can you share the client curl/openssl logs and the DNS answer from the affected host? My hunch: inspection is terminating TLS and either rewriting SNI or re-signing with their local CA (which the app doesn't trust).

maria_sales: Posted excerpts they sent (IPs redacted):
```
$ curl -v https://svc.globex.internal/ -o /dev/null
* Connected to 10.200.5.12 (10.200.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS alert, unknown CA
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
```
and from openssl:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.200.5.12:443 -servername svc.globex.internal -showcerts
...
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
no peer certificate available
---
```

kevin_netops: They also attached a tcpdump from the app subnet showing ClientHello SNI=svc.globex.internal, but the downstream server saw SNI=proxy-corp.globex.com. Vendor confirmed they rewrite SNI when doing TLS inspection unless bypass configured.

ash_se: That explains the unknown CA — their inspection device presents a re-signed cert chain using the firewall's CA. App hosts don't trust that CA so handshake fails. Two quick options: 1) Have their firewall bypass TLS inspection for the Private endpoint CIDR or FQDN (recommended for the POC). 2) Install the firewall CA into app host trust stores (not ideal for security/compliance). 3) We can offer a temporary config to accept their re-signed cert CN for the POC but that's a risk.

rachel_oncall: Also verify OCSP/CRL egress. If our endpoint expects stapling and can't reach OCSP responder, some stacks abort. Ask them to run `openssl s_client -connect 10.200.5.12:443 -servername svc.globex.internal -status` and `curl -I https://ocsp.<ca>.com/` from an app host.

maria_sales: I asked them to run those. They replied: OCSP reachable. They prefer bypassing inspection per-app but their central policy is strict. They asked whether we can do anything server-side to avoid this blocking their POC.

ash_se: Server-side options are limited without lowering verification. We could: a) temporarily accept the inspection CA by adding it to our allowed client cert list (requires infra change and security approval), b) provide a dedicated Private deployment with mutual TLS (client certs) so the inspector can't break the mTLS — that is a bigger lift. Estimate: option (a) ~1-2 dev-days + security review; option (b) >2 weeks and infra provisioning.

kevin_netops: If they can't change inspection, a practical POC workaround is to route app-subnet traffic through a bastion/proxy that does TLS passthrough to our endpoint (no inspection). They can NAT/proxy outbound only for the POC.

maria_sales: Customer asked about timeline for the quick bypass via firewall rules. They said they'd raise a change request but it may take 24-48h. They also want a written note of the security implications.

ash_se: I'll draft a short doc: what bypass means (no inspection for that flow), risks (traffic not inspected by DLP/AV), and roll-back steps. Also include the dev estimate if they want us to implement an acceptance of the inspection CA (and the legal sign-off required).

task-bot: Task created: POC-1995554321 — Investigate TLS inspection impact for Globex, ask for PCAP and openssl -status output. Assignee: ash_se. ETA: 48h.

maria_sales: They implemented a temporary bypass rule and confirmed at 17:35 that curl from app host returns 200. Customer will run functional tests tomorrow. Marking thread as 'monitoring' until sign-off. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
